_comment: Everything routing reads, one section per former file:
tags       the road graph's tag dictionary (`workers/routing/tags.py`; the app bundles its export)
rail_tags  the rail graph's, its own `id` so the two never join
profiles   routing engines, modes and their options (`workers/routing/profile.py`)
areas      national routing scopes and their extracts
vignettes  toll stickers by country (the app bundles the section whole)
Each section keeps its own `_comment`.
ROUTING TAG DICTIONARY – what of OSM travels to the phone.
The `<region>-routing.pmtiles` archive carries TAGS, not costs: the profile
is evaluated on the phone (`docs/navigation.md` §10, format in
`docs/routing-tiles.md`). So this list is also the SIZE LEVER.
`network` says WHAT IS A ROAD (which ways enter the graph), `keys` WHAT
TRAVELS ABOUT IT; a key doing both has `from_network: true`.
Three key kinds, an encoding difference: `values` (enumerated, an index in
the tile), `number` (integer without unit), `free` (string as in OSM).
Sizes stay strings: `12'6"` read as 12 would send a caravan under a bridge.
A value outside the list is dropped and counted by `tiles.py`.
`name` is for instructions and the first key cut when over budget.
`country` is not an OSM tag: the edge's country, for the vignette.
`speed_context` isn't either: which default limit applies (`routing/context.py`).
A new key goes LAST, so an older archive's indices still mean the same.
CHANGING THIS FILE CHANGES THE DICTIONARY `id` in every tile; archives with
different ids must never join (`workers/lint/routing-tiles.py`). The id is
hashed over the former Slovak names, so this translation didn't move it.
What makes a way a road: `highway`, plus ferries, lifts and platforms.

name.what: road name for the "turn onto…" instruction

ref.what: road number (D1, I/18) for the instruction and the sign

oneway.what: direction; `-1` runs against the way's node order

oneway:bicycle.what: a one-way that doesn't apply to bicycles

junction.what: roundabout – direction and the instruction ("third exit")

surface.what: surface – a cost for bicycles and caravans, not a ban

tracktype.what: track grade – `track` is one switch in the profile, the grade sets the cost

trail_visibility.what: whether the path is visible in the field

maxspeed.what: speed limit with its unit (`50`, `30 mph`)

maxheight:physical.what: real height when the sign is elsewhere

toll.what: toll for passing; a vignette is NOT one (`docs/navigation.md` §5)

service.what: kind of service road – a driveway isn't a car park aisle

layer.what: crossing level – a grade-separated crossing isn't a junction

country.what: the edge's country – input for the vignette, not an OSM tag

speed_context.what: which default limit of the country's law applies (`regulations/<country>.json` in traffic-signs) – from `workers/routing/context.py`, not an OSM tag

_comment: The values EVERY access key has (`access`, `foot`, `hgv`…), written once.
Routing tag dictionary for tracks – archive `<region>-rail-routing.pmtiles`.
The format of `tags`, another dictionary and so another `id`:
the rail network never joins the road one on the phone.
WHAT A USER ASKS OF NAVIGATION – in ONE place: each option once, with how it
translates into each engine. Read by `workers/routing/profile.py`, guarded by
`workers/lint/routing.py`.
Engines say the same thing in other words; a profile per engine would be two
truths that part silently. So what an engine CAN'T do is here too: `unsupported`
with a reason is the only way to SEE the hole; `profile.py --strict` fails on it,
otherwise it lands in `_unsupported` and on stderr.
Checked in Valhalla's source (master, August 2026): `exclude_highways` is exactly
`RoadClass::kMotorway`; `use_highways` scales the fixed `kHighwayFactor[]` table
(Motorway 1.0, Trunk 0.5, the rest 0.0), so it has NO effect on primary, secondary
and tertiary roads – that needs a patch (`docs/navigation.md`). GraphHopper's custom
model covers every option, `country` (the vignette) included.
A road CLASS is national law (the `ref` prefix), a TAG is the mapper's guess
(`highway=primary`); each option has both `osm` and `ref`, and one place – the
graph's tag transform – decides which holds.

valhalla.name: Valhalla
note: The only one of the two that runs OFFLINE ON THE PHONE – the reason it's first:
the app is built on downloading a region and opening it without signal.
The cost: the three road-class options for cars and per-country vignettes can't be said in it today.
valhalla.where: on the phone and on a server

graphhopper.name: GraphHopper
note: The custom model is DECLARATIVE and covers every option, `country` too, so
the vignette per country – without a line of C++. The cost: it's a JVM, so a
"with signal" route, not offline in the mountains.

bus.name: By bus (the vehicle, not a line)
note: NOT TRAVELLING BY BUS: `bus` is a VEHICLE in the engine – a car route with other
sizes and bans. Riding a line needs `transit` below, which is timetables (GTFS), not OSM.

pedestrian.name: On foot
note: DELIBERATELY UNFINISHED: three Valhalla options that make sense on a hiking map now
(`max_hiking_difficulty` is the SAC scale of `sac_scale`); more is a line here, not code.

transit.name: By public transport (bus, train)
note: IT STANDS ON TIMETABLES, NOT OSM – the one part the pipeline has no data for.
Without a GTFS source `transit` is an empty box, hence `needs_gtfs`; see `docs/navigation.md`.
ONLY DISCOURAGED, NOT EXCLUDED: `exclude_highways` is exactly `kMotorway`;
`use_highways: 0` raises the trunk cost via `kHighwayFactor` (0.5) but doesn't ban it –
and motorways get the same discouragement (1.0).

avoid_toll.name: Avoid toll roads
note: TOLL ≠ VIGNETTE: `toll=yes` is paid per passage (gate, tunnel, bridge); the vignette
has its own `vignettes` option – someone with one wants to avoid a country, not motorways.

unsupported: Valhalla can't say it at all today: `use_highways` scales the fixed
`kHighwayFactor[]` table, which is 0.0 for Primary – exactly zero effect. It needs a patch

note: `use_tracks: 0` discourages (scales `Use::kTrack` edges), `exclude_unpaved` bans
unpaved surfaces; together they fit "forest track", but a paved track passes the discouragement.

top_speed.name: Vehicle top speed
note: NOT A ROAD LIMIT, IT'S THE VEHICLE: "this is how fast I go" – it changes the TIME and
so which route wins; a caravan at 100 stops preferring the motorway by itself.

vehicle_height.name: Vehicle height
note: The other half of road restrictions: the underpass height is in OSM (`maxheight`) and in
the `roads` package to LOOK AT; here it's to USE – say the vehicle's height and the route avoids it.
The unit is metres, converted HERE: the tile keeps the sign's string (`3.8 m`, `12'6"`).

vehicle_weight.name: Vehicle weight
note: In Valhalla `weight` is a `truck` costing option; `auto` accepts and ignores it, so it
makes sense with `bus` and lorries.

vignettes.name: Motorway vignette per country

unsupported: Valhalla's costing has no notion of country (only `country_crossing_penalty`),
so "motorway allowed in Slovakia, not in Austria" can't be said. The same patch as for road classes.

note: THREE ANSWERS, NOT TWO: "I have one until 30 Sep", "I have none" and "this country sells
none" – in Poland motorways needn't be avoided because there is no vignette.
THE TRIP DATE decides, not today: a vignette may expire before next month's trip.

unsupported: The custom model knows no bicycle type – it's the profile choice (`bike`, `mtb`, `racingbike`).
Said otherwise – as a priority multiplier by `road_class`, not one number.
GraphHopper switches elevation on when building the graph (`graph.elevation`), not per route.

_comment: WHAT EXTENT THE ROUTING GRAPH IS BUILT FOR – another question than “which
map”, hence a lookup of its own and not another key in `areas.json`. Read by
`workers/routing/pbf.sh` and `graph.sh`, guarded by `workers/lint/navigation.py`.
THE GRAPH ISN'T SPLIT BY REGION like the map – not for convenience, it follows
from the brief. A vignette per country makes sense only when a route MAY cross
the border; one region's graph can't even take someone to Austria, so it can't
avoid lacking a vignette there. A map to look at and a graph to route on are
two extents of the same territory.
HENCE TWO OPTIONS, not one. Rule 7 (never download more than needed) stands
against the brief here: a cross-border route wants the neighbours, but they are
several GB of PBF and hours of building, while a runner has ~60 GB free and a
360 minute job cap. Whoever tries routing or drives at home builds
`slovensko`; whoever goes to Austria pays for `slovensko_susedia`.
TIMES AND SIZES ARE TO BE FILLED IN FROM THE FIRST RUN. They're deliberately
not estimated: a number in a comment here means measured. `graph.sh` prints
them into the run summary and the package's `contents.json`.
_pbf: The PBF source is the same as the map's – osm.fr (`OSMFR_BASE`), since the
whole pipeline goes there and one source shouldn't be doubled. Paths go

slovensko.name: Slovensko
note: The default. A route doesn't cross the border, so the `vignettes` option only
means SK in this graph – and `profile.py` says so, since it takes countries
from `vignettes`, not from the graph.

slovensko_susedia.name: Slovensko a susedia
note: THIS IS THE COSTLY RUN and the only form in which a vignette per country fully
makes sense. Poland and Ukraine are the biggest pieces and a trip to Austria
needs neither – if it won't fit the runner's caps, the right answer is ANOTHER
ENTRY here (e.g. `slovensko_at_cz`), not a quiet trim of this one.
THE NAME IS A PROMISE ABOUT EXTENT (rule 2): if a state were quietly dropped,
the package would still be called `…_susedia` and a route in it would end at
the border without explanation.

cesko.name: Česko
note: The node order the Czech regions share, as `slovensko` for Slovakia.

rakusko.name: Rakúsko
note: The node order the Austrian regions share, as `slovensko` for Slovakia.

_comment: WHERE A MOTORWAY VIGNETTE IS NEEDED – and which roads it covers. The lookup for the
`vignettes` option in `profiles`; read by `workers/routing/profile.py`,
guarded by `workers/lint/routing.py`, copied whole into the app.
Only what doesn't change per trip: whether the country sells one and where it applies.
Whether the USER has one is app state, mixed in by `profile.py`.
A VIGNETTE ISN'T A TOLL: it's paid for TIME on a network, a toll per PASSAGE (`toll=yes`),
hence two options, `avoid_toll` and `vignettes`.
These data change by law, not by OSM, so every entry has a primary `source` and a
`state`: `verified` (compared with the source, dated) or `unverified` (must be checked
before the app trusts it). `required_on` are OSM classes, which the graph knows.

_states.verified: compared with the primary source – `verified_on` says when
_states.unverified: UNVERIFIED. While this stands, it must not reach the app as fact.

SK.name: Slovakia
notes: The vignette covers vehicles up to 3.5 t; above that a distance toll applies, another question.
Some motorway sections are exempt (city bypasses) – that needs `toll=no` on them in OSM;
until then the detour is sometimes needless.

AT.name: Austria
notes: ON TOP of the vignette some sections have a section toll (Brenner, Tauern, Arlberg):
`toll=yes`, handled by `avoid_toll` – the vignette doesn't pay those tunnels.

HU.name: Hungary
notes: Hungary also sells COUNTY vignettes, so "I have one" isn't one answer for the country;
this lookup treats a vignette as national – a county one gets a route that allows too much.

CH.name: Switzerland
notes: No short-term vignette exists – only an annual one.

PL.name: Poland
PL.system: no vignette; toll per passage on some motorways
notes: THIS IS THE THIRD ANSWER, not "I have none": motorways needn't be avoided at all;
tolled sections are `toll=yes` and belong to `avoid_toll`.
